summary: William Knighton (1824–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as headmaster at the Norman Seminary, Colombo (~1845–1849), as Lecturer in History and Logic at Presidency University (1846), and held a post in the Indian Civil Service.

William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned an M.S. at Caltech and a Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, holding posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University.

William Lee-Warner (1846–1914) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Rugby School and St John's College (B.A. 1869), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1869–1895), and became a Fellow of the University of Mumbai (~1877).

William Linwood (1817–1878) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Christ Church, Oxford (B.A. 1839, M.A. ~1842). He taught at Shrewsbury School (~1841–1842) and served as a public examiner at the University of Oxford in 1850.

William Logan (1841–1914) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1858–1861), served in the Madras Civil Service (1862–1888), and was a Fellow at the University of Madras (1882).

William M. Bodiford (b. 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale (Ph.D. under Stanley Weinstein), later teaching at UCLA from ~1993 until becoming Professor Emeritus in ~2021.

William M. Gorvine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Connecticut College and an M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano (attested 2006).
William MacColin Kirkpatrick (1878–1953) was an Indologist. He was educated at Bishop Cotton School and served in the Indian Civil Service.

William Markby (1829–1914) was a legal scholar and Indologist educated at Merton College and Oxford (D.C.L.). He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (~1877–1878) and held posts at Oxford, including Reader in Indian Law (1878–1900).

William McCulloch (1856–1928) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He was educated at institutions including the University of Edinburgh and served as Principal of Chinsurah Theological College in 1886.

William McGrath is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (2010–2017). After a post at Virginia, he became an Assistant Professor at New York University in 2021.

William Montgomery McGovern (1897–1964) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Berlin, Sorbonne, and Oxford (D.Phil. ~1922), he held posts at SOAS (1918–1924), the Field Museum (1927), and Northwestern University (Professor from 1929).

William Nassau Lees (1825–1889) was an Indology, linguistics, and history scholar educated at Trinity College Dublin. He served as Principal and Professor at Aliah University (~1853–1870) and Secretary to the Board of Examiners at Fort William (~1855–1870).
William P. Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his M.A. and doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2006) at the University of California, Los Angeles.

William Pettigrew (1869–1943) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Ardington Aborigines Mission Training Centre (~1888–1890) and served as a missionary with the American Baptist Missionary Union beginning in 1894.

William Price (1780–1830) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served on Gore Ouseley's Mission to Persia (1811–1812) and taught languages at Fort William College from 1813, becoming Professor in 1824.

William R. Hutchison (1930–2005) worked in religious studies and history. He studied at Oxford and Yale (Ph.D. ~1956) and taught at Yale, Hunter College, American University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Harvard University (from 1968).

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin, Michigan, and Chicago (Ph.D. ~1973), he held posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) was a linguist and religious scholar educated at Muskingum and Yale (Ph.D. 1875 under William Dwight Whitney). He held professorships at Yale and elsewhere, became President of the University of Chicago (1891–1906), and headed Bradley University.

William Reeve (1794–1850) was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (~1815–1824, ~1827–1834) and was later minister at Oswestry Congregational Church (1836–1843).
